attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing analytic estimate is the positivity-compatible trace/collar bound for nonlocal gauge-invariant observables and renormalized local composites as their support approaches the reflection plane. In Yang-Mills this is not a harmless density argument because reflected products can create contact terms at \(t=0\), perimeter/cusp divergences for Wilson loops, and renormalization mixing for local gauge-invariant composites.
steps: Fix a finite family \(F_1,\dots,F_n\in\mathcal A_+\) and coefficients \(c\). Choose collar approximants \(F_i^{\delta}=R_\delta F_i\in\mathcal A_+^{\delta}\).

For each \(\delta>0\), regulated reflection positivity gives \(Q_{a,L}(F^{\delta},c)\ge0\). Collar convergence then yields \(Q_S(F^{\delta},c)=\lim_{a,L}Q_{a,L}(F^{\delta},c)\ge0\). This part is formal and valid once the RG topology controls separated reflected probes.

Use the cutoff-uniform estimate \(|Q_{a,L}(F,c)-Q_{a,L}(F^{\delta},c)|\le C(F,c)\omega_F(\delta)\) and pass to the limit in \((a,L)\) on both terms. This would imply \(|Q_S(F,c)-Q_S(F^{\delta},c)|\le C(F,c)\omega_F(\delta)\).

Let \(\delta\downarrow0\). Since each \(Q_S(F^{\delta},c)\ge0\) and the difference tends to zero, conclude \(Q_S(F,c)\ge0\). Thus the OS cone is reached for the full positive-time algebra rather than only for observables separated from the reflection plane.

The derivation also shows necessity in practice: if an RG topology fails to make the maps \(S\mapsto Q_S(F,c)\) continuous or lower-semicontinuous, the closed-cone step has no valid input even though every cutoff theory is positive.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument proves a conditional bridge theorem, not Yang-Mills OS positivity, until Balaban-style or lattice RG bounds are shown to dominate the reflected collar seminorms uniformly in the cutoff. The unproved part is exactly where a falsifier could live: an observable may be approximable in ordinary distribution topology but not in the OS quadratic topology.

assumptions: For every cutoff pair \((a,L)\), \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\ge0\) for all finite \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+\) after applying the fixed embedding \(J_{a,L}\).
For every \(\delta>0\), every finite \(F_i\in\mathcal A_+^{\delta}\), and every coefficient vector \(c\), the limit \(\lim_{a\downarrow0,L\uparrow\infty}Q_{a,L}(F,c)=Q_S(F,c)\) exists.

There are seminorms \(\rho_m\) on \(\mathcal A_+\) and a modulus \(\omega_F(\delta)\to0\) such that the cutoff reflected quadratic errors between \(F_i\) and \(R_\delta F_i\) are bounded uniformly in \((a,L)\) after the renormalized observables are embedded.
The convergence topology is strong enough to pass mixed reflected forms \(S_{a,L}((\Theta R_\delta F_i)F_j)\), not only unmixed Euclidean moments.
Reflection preserves the regulator and the embeddings commute with reflection on the nose or up to an error already absorbed by \(\omega_F(\delta)\).
definitions: source object: a net \(S_{a,L}\) of regulated gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals on a fixed abstract positive-time algebra \(\mathcal A_+\), with embeddings \(J_{a,L}:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_{a,L,+}\), reflection \(\Theta\), and finite OS quadratic forms \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\).

target object: a continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) on the same locked gauge-invariant algebra whose reflected finite quadratic forms \(Q_S(F,c)=\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j S((\Theta F_i)F_j)\) are nonnegative, hence valid input for OS Hilbert-space reconstruction.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, controlled not merely by weak distributional convergence but by convergence of the reflected quadratic probes used in OS positivity.

same-theory condition: the abstract observables \(F\in\mathcal A_+\) are identified before and after cutoff removal by product-, involution-, reflection-, and gauge-invariant embeddings \(J_{a,L}\); no gauge fixing, quotient replacement, or change from Wilson/composite gauge-invariant probes to a different test algebra is allowed.
\(\mathcal A_+^{\delta}\) is the collar subalgebra generated by smeared Wilson loops, smeared curvature polynomials, or other gauge-invariant probes whose supports lie in \(t\ge\delta\).

A positivity-compatible collar approximation is a family \(R_\delta:\mathcal A_+\to\mathcal A_+^{\delta}\) such that \(R_\delta F\to F\) in the observable topology and the reflected quadratic error is uniformly small at the regulated and continuum levels.

equations.label: regulated OS form on locked algebra
equations.valid_when: Valid for every finite positive-time gauge-invariant family if the regulator action and measure are reflection-positive and the embeddings do not change the observable algebra.

equations.label: collar convergence
equations.valid_when: Valid when the RG cutoff-removal topology dominates all reflected finite quadratic forms with a positive distance from the reflection plane.

equations.label: uniform collar trace estimate
equations.valid_when: Valid only if the multiscale bounds control reflection-plane approach, including contact terms of renormalized gauge-invariant composite observables.

equations.label: closed positivity passage
equations.valid_when: Valid after the two limits are justified by collar convergence plus the uniform trace estimate; otherwise this equation is exactly where a falsifier can enter.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any gauge-invariant observable family \(F_i\) with support approaching the reflection plane for which \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)-Q_{a,L}(R_\delta F,c)\) has no cutoff-uniform modulus tending to zero; then positivity may hold on every collar algebra but fail to be established on the full OS test algebra.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the remaining bridge from formal closed-cone closure to a concrete analytic domination theorem: prove positivity away from the reflection plane by convergence, then extend to observables touching the plane through a uniform trace/collar approximation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Collar-to-trace OS positivity bridge: let \(\mathcal A_+\) be the locked gauge-invariant positive-time observable algebra and let \(\mathcal A_+^{\delta}\subset \mathcal A_+\) denote observables whose Euclidean time support is at distance at least \(\delta>0\) from the reflection plane. If regulated Schwinger forms \(S_{a,L}\) are reflection-positive on the corresponding regulated algebra, converge on all collar-separated reflected quadratic forms, and satisfy a uniform positivity-compatible collar approximation estimate as \(\delta\downarrow0\), then the continuum Schwinger functional \(S\) is OS-positive on all of \(\mathcal A_+\).

assumptions: The observable algebra and reflection map are fixed independently of the cutoff.
The cone \(\mathcal C_{OS}=\{S:Q_S(F,c)\ge0\text{ for all finite }(F,c)\}\) is tested on the same finite families at cutoff and in the limit.
Convergence of \(S_{a,L}\) to \(S\) is interpreted as convergence in \(\tau_{RG}\).
definitions: \(\tau_{RG}\) is the topology delivered by multiscale compactness and renormalized Schwinger bounds.
\(\tau_{OS}\) is the initial topology generated by all finite reflected quadratic maps \(S\mapsto Q_S(F,c)\) on the locked algebra.
Domination \(\tau_{RG}\succeq\tau_{OS}\) means every OS quadratic probe is continuous along RG-convergent subnets.

equations.label: topological domination criterion
equations.valid_when: Valid for the fixed algebra when the maps \(Q(\cdot;F,c)\) are among the scalar observables whose continuity defines \(\tau_{OS}\).

equations.label: closed cone identity
equations.valid_when: Valid because each finite OS inequality is a closed half-line condition once the corresponding quadratic map is continuous.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If \(\tau_{RG}\) controls only unreflected Euclidean moments or only separated non-gauge-invariant fields, then a sequence may converge in \(\tau_{RG}\) while an uncontrolled OS quadratic coordinate becomes negative in the limit; that is a topological falsifier of the bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma says the formal closed-cone argument is complete once the RG topology is proved to dominate \(\tau_{OS}\); it prevents spending effort on a second proof of cone closure.
candidate_lemmas.statement: OS-probe domination equivalence: for a fixed same-theory gauge-invariant algebra, reflection positivity is preserved along every reflection-positive cutoff net converging to \(S\) if and only if every finite OS quadratic functional \(S\mapsto Q_S(F,c)\) is lower-semicontinuous, equivalently continuous for scalar convergence, in the actual RG cutoff-removal topology.

assumptions: Gauge-invariant generators separate the intended continuum Yang-Mills law sufficiently for the reconstruction target.
Renormalizations of local composites are fixed by same continuum normalization conditions before positivity is tested.
No positivity proof is allowed to discard observables that are needed later for the mass-gap or Wightman reconstruction target.
definitions: The locked algebra may be generated by traced holonomies of piecewise smooth loops and by renormalized smeared local gauge-invariant composites, completed in the chosen test topology.
Reflection compatibility means \(J_{a,L}(\Theta F)=\Theta_{a,L}J_{a,L}(F)\) for all generators, extended to the completed algebra.
Algebraic consistency means products, adjoints, Euclidean covariance on the subgroup preserving the cutoff limit, and gauge invariance survive the embeddings.

equations.label: reflection-compatible embedding
equations.valid_when: Valid if reflection is exact on lattice Wilson-loop observables or if the regulator error is dominated by the same collar estimate.

equations.label: same quadratic form across cutoff
equations.valid_when: Valid as a test of the same theory only when \(F_i\) denote the same abstract physical observables for all \((a,L)\).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a proof that obtains positivity only after replacing Wilson-loop/composite observables by gauge-fixed field coordinates or by an algebra that omits reflection-plane limits needed for OS reconstruction.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a guard lemma: it rules out an artificial proof where OS positivity survives because the test algebra was weakened or changed during cutoff removal.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Same-theory lock for gauge-invariant OS tests: the closed-cone positivity bridge proves positivity for Yang-Mills only if the cutoff observables, collar approximants, and continuum observables are related by a single reflection-compatible gauge-invariant algebra, not by cutoff-dependent gauge choices or by a smaller algebra selected after the limit.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the available RG bounds cannot be upgraded from separated Euclidean correlations to reflected collar quadratic forms, or if reflection-plane contact terms require changing the observable algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves a cutoff-uniform estimate for \(|Q_{a,L}(F,c)-Q_{a,L}(R_\delta F,c)|\) on a generating family of Wilson-loop and smeared local gauge-invariant observables, with \(omega_F(\delta)\to0\), while preserving the same-theory embeddings.
control_decision.reason: The branch remains productive because it has converted the preservation problem into a specific analytic estimate whose failure would be a real falsifier. Further work should not reprove closed-cone closure; it should test reflected collar domination on concrete gauge-invariant generators.

dependency_updates.description: Reduced to a conditional theorem: \(\tau_{RG}\succeq\tau_{OS}\) plus a collar-to-trace estimate implies OS positivity. The closed-cone component is valid and formal; the estimate near the reflection plane is the nonformal part.

The algebra must be locked before cutoff removal and must include the observables later needed for reconstruction. Positivity on a smaller or changed algebra is no longer accepted as evidence for the same Yang-Mills theory.

The topology must control finite reflected quadratic forms, first on collar-separated probes and then through a uniform trace/contact-term extension. Ordinary weak convergence of Schwinger distributions is insufficient unless it implies these seminorms.

falsifiers: A concrete falsifier would be a sequence of gauge-invariant Wilson-loop observables whose loops approach or touch the reflection plane while the reflected quadratic error has a cutoff-dependent cusp or perimeter counterterm with no \(\delta\to0\) modulus.

Another falsifier is RG convergence that is valid for separated Euclidean correlations but fails for mixed reflected products \((\Theta F_i)F_j\), so the topology is too weak to identify \(Q_S(F,c)\) as a limit of \(Q_{a,L}(F,c)\).

A same-theory falsifier occurs if positivity is proved only after replacing the locked gauge-invariant algebra by a gauge-fixed or quotient algebra that is not known to reconstruct the intended Yang-Mills observables.

Reflection positivity might be valid for the lattice transfer matrix but not for the renormalized continuum Schwinger functions if counterterms needed for cutoff removal are not reflection-even or do not commute with the embeddings.
A trace-extension falsifier occurs if collar positivity holds for every \(\delta>0\) but the limiting quadratic form at \(\delta=0\) acquires an uncontrolled negative contact term.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 170 identifies the next non-tautological lemma: OS positivity should be proved first on a collar algebra away from the reflection plane and then extended by a uniform trace/collar estimate. This separates three layers: the closed cone is valid in \(\tau_{OS}\), RG convergence must dominate collar-separated reflected probes, and Yang-Mills-specific analysis must control reflection-plane contact, cusp, and composite-renormalization terms. The word 'same theory' has become a mathematical condition on embeddings, not a slogan.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out the collar estimate first for a minimal generating probe: two traced holonomies contained in positive-time slabs \(t\ge\delta\), then let one loop approach the reflection plane. Track whether lattice reflection positivity and known Wilson-loop perimeter/cusp renormalizations give a cutoff-uniform modulus or expose the first concrete obstruction.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
